title: Leads
source: Read via Notion MCP notion-fetch on 2026-11-14 and re-read 2026-11-17 from a live CRM. Data source ids are not carried and are NOT portable: a deploy creates new ones.

Status.writer: Hub sets New on create, then people; the Hub sets In progress at the first reply sent, Spam on the owner's click, New on its Undo (P97)

Source.note: option Email carries the description 'The first message arrived by email, not through the website form.'; a missing Email option stops Hub writing

Client.writer: Hub (at the first reply sent to the lead, P97)

Conversation summary.note: not used on Leads by the pack; kept for the email-assistant contract

Brand.note: The project key of the lead's origin (decision 0053): which site or product the lead came from. Leads keeps `Brand` (the other databases use `Projects`): the integration writes it (django_notion matches the backend's project key to the option with the same key: lower case, letters and digits only), the silence check filters on it, and Clients' `Project signals` reads it. The options are named like the project's `## Brands` rows; `hub install --only notion.projects` adds a missing one. A missing option leaves Brand empty, never stops the form. One lead can carry several brands; `Other` is no project.
Brand.description: The project key of the lead's origin: the site or product it came from. Written by the integration; options named like the Hub's ## Brands rows.

noteVsPack: Read live 2026-11-17 (CRM: SaaS, Leads moved to the top level of the teamspace). Brand exists now (multi_select, project-specific options). Source and Status are type select (not status). Ad-tracking columns (flag ads) are written by the owner's backend once mapped; deploy them only when the project runs ads. The writer column says 'Hub' for what the integration writes: in the pack 'Hub' means any writer that follows @docs/core/21-leads.md.
